## Context 

We shared our contribution on the WG mailing list (cf. [thread](https://lists.aaif.io/g/wg-identity-trust/topic/121848020)). Two separate participants mentioned about issues in WG. So I am posting a summary here for discussion. 

## Contribution 

https://www.researchgate.net/publication/417343302_EarlyAttestationTschuss_EAT

## End of Life of Early Attestation

Based on our findings:

1. **Privasys** has [declared end of life](https://github.com/Privasys/go/commit/91195564d435a374e45d485d39edbc6cf8235901) of its early attestation implementations in Go and archived those to move to standard (post-handshake) attestation.
2. **Privasys** has [declared end of life](https://github.com/Privasys/rustls/commit/c39f7107dffd710c5087b1885a71b4bb8ff2de31) of its early attestation implementations in Rustls and archived those to move to standard (post-handshake) attestation.
3. **Cocos AI** has [declared end of life](https://github.com/ultravioletrs/cocos/releases/tag/v0.9.0) of its early attestation and migrated to standard (post-handshake) attestation.
4. **CCC** has [declared end of life](https://github.com/CCC-Attestation/attested-tls-poc/pull/60) of its early attestation reference implementation and archived the repo.
5. The authors of [**draft-fossati-tls-attestation-10**](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-fossati-tls-attestation/) have withdrawn it because of our discovered vulnerabilities.

## Still Vulnerable 

From the lens of cryptography, the vulnerable draft [**draft-fossati-seat-early-attestation-09**](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-fossati-seat-early-attestation/) essentially has the same protocol as the withdrawn draft-fossati-tls-attestation-10, except that public key is appended with transcript hash up to ServerHello message. In our analysis, it does not help much.

**Edgeless Systems Contrast** has applied some of our proposed mitigations but it still follows the withdrawn draft-fossati-tls-attestation-10 and remains vulnerable based on our formal analysis.

**Meta** still follows the withdrawn draft-fossati-tls-attestation-10 and remains vulnerable based on our formal analysis.

## Acknowledgements of Vulnerabilities

See email for concrete references:

1. We submitted confidential vulnerability report together with formal analysis (and in some cases regression tests) to repo owner and maintainers following their disclosure processes. The maintainers reviewed, accepted, and published GitHub Security Advisories (GHSAs). Except for one CVE, they themselves requested the CVEs from GitHub.
2. GitHub (acting as CNA) and VulnCheck (acting as CNA) reviewed, accepted, and published as CVE records.
3. NIST reviewed, accepted, and published as CVE records in NVD.
4. ENISA reviewed, accepted, and published as EUVD records.
5. China Information Technology Security Evaluation Center (CNITSEC) reviewed, accepted, and published as CNNVD records.
6. Many other reputable international vulnerability database managers similarly reviewed, accepted, and published corresponding records in their vulnerability databases. I need not name each and every one here.
7. The vulnerabilities have been shared with the related communities: 
    1. [Global Alliance for Genomics and Health](https://groups.google.com/a/ga4gh.org/g/gif-open-tre-members/c/hqx1P4bcTT0)
    2. [IRTF UFMRG](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/ufmrg/8RPCf502JFmsBui5rUZw38l76Rk/)
    3. [IRTF CFRG](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/cfrg/_Ol3Ft4PZFrg47Nujxr_xvRgoq4/)
    4. [Confidential Computing Consortium](https://lists.confidentialcomputing.io/g/attestation/message/343)
    5. [AAIF Security and Privacy](https://lists.aaif.io/g/wg-security-privacy/topic/spaa_meeting_notes_for/121831017)
    6. [Open Compute Project security](https://ocp-all.groups.io/g/OCP-Security/message/1279)
    7. [Linux Plumbers Conference](https://lpc.events/event/20/contributions/2585/)
    8. [RIPE](https://ripe93.ripe.net/programme/meeting-plan/sessions/137/GJXMGP/)

I'm surely missing a few communities, but I hope that gives sufficient idea to the WG. None of the CVEs have been refuted by even a single person in the wider community to the best of my and my co-author's knowledge at this point in time.
